# SMART — Field Reference

SMART (**S**omatic **M**utation **A**nnotation and **R**eporting **T**ool) integrates
annotations from multiple sources into a single output table. This page describes every
field the pipeline is configured to produce — what it contains, where it comes from,
which version of that tool or database produced it, and which of the three output files
it reaches.

## What is on this page

`Config.yaml` describes **427 columns** by name, grouped below into
15 sources, plus **36 patterns** covering the indexed columns whose
names are only known once a variant has been annotated:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Columns described by name | 427 |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;of which reach an output file | 369 |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;of which are dropped (`tier: drop`) | 58 |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;in the Tier 3 clinical sheet (`tier: 3`) | 92 |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;in the Tier 2 sheet only (`tier: 2`) | 273 |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;in the Tier 1 MAF only (`tier: 1`) | 4 |
| Patterns covering indexed columns | 36 |

A single run produces more columns than this: the patterns expand to as many columns as
the data needs, and columns a VCF documents for itself need no entry here. The Tier 1
MAF of a real run has carried around 1,000.

## What the tiers mean

Every entry carries a `tier`, and the tier decides which of the three output files the
column appears in. The table below is read from the routing loop in
`scripts/post_analysis.py`, which is the only thing that decides it:

| `tier` in the configuration | `Final_result_tier3.tsv` | `Final_result_tier2.tsv` | `Final_result_tier1.maf` | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `3` | Yes | Yes | Yes | The clinical set: the narrowest, most interpretable columns. |
| `2` | &ndash; | Yes | Yes | The bioinformatician set: supporting evidence and the raw scores behind Tier 3. |
| `1` | &ndash; | &ndash; | Yes | Everything else that is kept. <code>tier: 1</code> is also what any unrecognised value behaves as, and is the default for a column with no entry at all. |
| `drop` | &ndash; | &ndash; | &ndash; | Removed from every output — intermediates, duplicated columns and the JSON blobs that have already been expanded into columns of their own. |

Two consequences are worth stating plainly, because they are easy to get backwards:

- **Tier 3 is the narrow clinical sheet and Tier 2 contains it.** A `tier: 3` column is
  written to the Tier 2 sheet as well, so Tier 2 is a superset of Tier 3, and the Tier 1
  MAF is a superset of both.
- **Tier 1 is not a curated set, and is not a sheet.** It is where a column lands when
  nothing else claims it, including a column with no entry in the configuration at all,
  and such a column appears in neither TSV. To put a column in front of a clinical
  scientist, give it `tier: 3`; to give it to a bioinformatician only, `tier: 2`.

## Field reference

Within each source, columns are ordered by the tier they reach — Tier 3 first, dropped
columns last — and alphabetically within a tier.

<tr data-field="SpliceAI_pred_DS_DG" data-source="SpliceAI" data-tier="3"><td><code>SpliceAI_pred_DS_DG</code></td><td>SpliceAI delta score predicting the probability that the variant creates a new splice donor site (donor gain). <tr data-field="SpliceAI_pred_DS_DL" data-source="SpliceAI" data-tier="3"><td><code>SpliceAI_pred_DS_DL</code></td><td>SpliceAI delta score predicting the probability that the variant disrupts an existing splice donor site (donor loss). <tr data-field="SpliceAI_cutoff" data-source="SpliceAI" data-tier="2"><td><code>SpliceAI_cutoff</code></td><td>Decision threshold applied to SpliceAI delta scores to classify variants as likely splice-altering. <tr data-field="SpliceAI_pred_DP_AG" data-source="SpliceAI" data-tier="2"><td><code>SpliceAI_pred_DP_AG</code></td><td>Predicted distance in base pairs between the variant position and the newly created splice acceptor site (acceptor gain). <tr data-field="SpliceAI_pred_DP_DL" data-source="SpliceAI" data-tier="2"><td><code>SpliceAI_pred_DP_DL</code></td><td>Predicted distance in base pairs between the variant position and the disrupted splice donor site (donor loss). <h3 id="source-revel">REVEL <small>(1 column)</small></h3>

<tbody>
<tr data-field="REVEL" data-source="REVEL" data-tier="3"><td><code>REVEL</code></td><td>Rare Exome Variant Ensemble Learner score predicting pathogenicity of missense variants (https://sites.google.com/site/revelgenomics/). REVEL scores the amino-acid substitution, not the transcript structure, so it transfers between transcripts that give the same change. Its source file records one transcript per score and those are older Ensembl identifiers, so the plugin&#x27;s default transcript-matched lookup returned nothing for variants annotated on a newer transcript -- BRAF V600E among them, where the file holds 0.931 for ENST00000288602 while the pipeline reports ENST00000646891. The plugin is therefore run with no_match=1: the score is for the substitution, and where the transcript differs from the one reported, the amino-acid change is the same</td><td class="src">REVEL</td><td class="ver"><small>1.3</small></td><td><span class="badge t3">3</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</div>

## Columns documented by pattern

OncoKB returns its treatment, diagnostic and prognostic implications as JSON arrays, and
`scripts/post_analysis.py` expands each array element into columns of its own —
`ONCOKB_TX_0_level`, `ONCOKB_TX_1_level`, and so on for as many implications as the
variant has. How many there are is a property of the data, so these columns cannot be
listed by name in advance.

They are documented by `fnmatch` pattern instead. At run time
`scripts/vcf_metadata.py` (`resolve()`) tries the exact column name against the entries
above first, and only then walks the patterns in order, taking the metadata of the first
one that matches. A column matching none of either is reported as undocumented by
`report_undocumented_columns()` and still appears in the output — it simply carries no
description in the metadata header row.

The `*` stands for the array index. These are patterns, not column names: the table
below is reproduced from the configuration exactly, and is not expanded into concrete
column names, because the expansion depends on the run.

<div class="warn">
<strong>One gap, stated rather than hidden.</strong>
<code>scripts/post_analysis.py</code> expands three OncoKB arrays in this way:
treatments into <code>ONCOKB_TX_*</code>, diagnostic implications into
<code>ONCOKB_DIAG_*</code> and prognostic implications into
<code>ONCOKB_PROG_*</code>. The configuration has patterns for the first two
only, so the <code>ONCOKB_PROG_*</code> columns reach the Tier 1 MAF with no
description, source or version, and
<code>report_undocumented_columns()</code> lists them when a run finishes. They
are absent from the table below because the configuration does not describe
them &mdash; not because the columns do not exist. Adding
<code>ONCOKB_PROG_*</code> patterns to the configuration documents them and
removes this notice.
</div>

## Where a column's description, source and version come from

The table above is the configuration. A run can be more specific than the
configuration, and where it is, the run wins: a VCF documents its own fields in its
`##INFO`/`##FORMAT` headers, for the exact versions that produced them, and
`scripts/vcf_metadata.py` harvests those headers and prefers them. The OncoKB columns
likewise take the data version observed in the run. `docs/field_provenance.md` sets out
the precedence in full.

So the second header row of a Tier 2 or Tier 3 sheet may carry a more precise source or
version than this page does. Where they differ, the sheet is describing the run and this
page is describing the configuration.

<script>
function filterTable() {
  const search = document.getElementById('search').value.toLowerCase();
  const src    = document.getElementById('src-filter').value;
  const tier   = document.getElementById('tier-filter').value;
  let visible = 0;
  document.querySelectorAll('.group').forEach(group => {
    let shown = 0;
    group.querySelectorAll('tbody tr').forEach(row => {
      const text    = row.textContent.toLowerCase();
      const rowSrc  = row.dataset.source || '';
      const rowTier = row.dataset.tier   || '';
      const match = (!search || text.includes(search))
                 && (!src    || rowSrc === src)
                 && (!tier   || rowTier === tier);
      row.classList.toggle('hidden', !match);
      if (match) { shown++; visible++; }
    });
    group.classList.toggle('hidden', shown === 0);
  });
  const total = document.querySelectorAll('.group tbody tr').length;
  document.getElementById('result-count').textContent =
    visible + ' of ' + total + ' entries shown';
}
filterTable();
</script>
